claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16 years old, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who is 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, who is 13 years old.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually - I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's important information.

**Are you a Crown servant, or do you live in a country where you can still get Child Benefit?** 

For context, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant working abroad. Could you tell me which country you currently live in?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not a Crown servant, no. I'm just living abroad - not in any special capacity or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Which country are you currently living in?**

This will help me determine whether you may still be eligible for Child Benefit while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into specifics, but it's not one of those countries where you can still claim UK benefits. Just a regular country abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on what you've told me, I need to let you know that according to UK Child Benefit rules, you generally need to **live in the UK** to qualify for Child Benefit.

There are some exceptions for people who live abroad - specifically if you're a Crown servant (which you've confirmed you're not) or if you live in certain designated countries - but if you're living in a country where these exceptions don't apply, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit.

**Just to confirm: are you currently residing outside the UK and don't have Crown servant status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I'm living outside the UK and I'm not a Crown servant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have what I need to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit.

## Result: Not Eligible

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex at this time.

**Why?** The key requirement for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. Although Alex is the right age (13 years old), the residency requirement is not met since you're living abroad in a country where UK Child Benefit exceptions don't apply.

**If your circumstances change** - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you have any questions or if your situation changes in the future, feel free to reach out.
